short_description.id: Zennyo Ryūō adalah naga pembawa hujan dalam mitologi Jepang yang menurut tradisi Buddha dimunculkan Kūkai pada lomba doa hujan tahun 824 di Kyoto.
short_description.en: Zennyo Ryūō is a rain-bringing dragon of Japanese mythology that, in Buddhist tradition, Kūkai made appear in the 824 rainmaking contest in Kyoto.

long_description.id: Zennyo Ryūō (善如龍王 atau 善女龍王) adalah raja naga pembawa hujan dalam mitologi Jepang dan salah satu raja naga yang menjadi sasaran doa meminta hujan. Menurut tradisi Buddha Jepang, pendeta Kūkai memunculkannya pada tahun 824 di Istana Kekaisaran Kyoto selama lomba doa hujan yang terkenal. Kemunculannya yang paling terkenal terjadi di Shinsen'en, saat Kūkai bersaing dengan pendeta Shubin.
long_description.en: Zennyo Ryūō (善如龍王 or 善女龍王) is a rain-bringing dragon king in Japanese mythology and one of the dragon kings who are objects of rain-praying. According to Japanese Buddhist tradition, the priest Kūkai made him appear in 824 at the Kyoto Imperial Palace during a famous rainmaking contest. His best-known appearance came at the Shinsen'en, when Kūkai competed with the priest Shubin.

long_description.id: Dalam versi artikel bahasa Jepang, Shubin yang iri mengurung dewa naga seluruh negeri dalam guci, tetapi Zennyo Ryūō lolos dan dipanggil dari kolam di India lalu menurunkan hujan lebat ke seluruh negeri. Ia dikatakan keluarga Anavatapta, salah satu Delapan Raja Naga; sebagian versi menyebut ia datang dari Gunung Murō. Naskah 御遺告 tahun 835 menggambarkannya sebagai ular emas kecil yang menunggangi kepala naga yang lebih besar.
long_description.en: In the Japanese article's version, the envious Shubin shut the dragon gods of the whole land in a pitcher, but Zennyo Ryūō escaped, was summoned from a pond in India and sent heavy rain over the whole country. He is said to belong to the family of Anavatapta, one of the Eight Dragon Kings; some versions say he came from Mount Murō. The 835 text 御遺告 describes him as a small golden snake riding on the head of a larger dragon.

long_description.id: Konon Zennyo atau Zentatsu tinggal di gua naga di Gunung Murō, Prefektur Nara, tempat kuno pemujaan naga dan upacara pemanggil hujan. Dalam Genkō Shakusho, ia muncul sebagai perempuan cantik yang mengaku Naga Zennyo dan memperlihatkan cakar raksasa. Seni sering menggambarkannya sebagai naga kecil, kadang sebagai manusia berekor naga; ia dipuja di kuil di Shinsen'en.
long_description.en: Zennyo or Zentatsu supposedly lived in a dragon cave on Mount Murō, Nara Prefecture, an ancient site of dragon worship and rainmaking ceremonies. In the Genkō Shakusho he appears as a beautiful woman who names herself the Dragon Zennyo and reveals a huge claw. Art often depicts him as a small dragon, sometimes as a human with a dragon's tail; he is worshipped at a shrine in the Shinsen'en.

description.en: He is a rain-bringing dragon; in the 824 story he is summoned and is said to have sent heavy rain over the whole country.

learning_questions.id: Mengapa raja naga begitu sering dipanggil dalam upacara meminta hujan?
learning_questions.en: Why might dragon kings so often be called upon in rain-praying rites?

claims.quote: Zennyo Ryūō (善如龍王 or 善女龍王; lit. "goodness-like dragon-king" or "goodness woman dragon-king", respectively) is a rain-god dragon in Japanese mythology.

statement.id: Zennyo Ryūō adalah dewa naga yang berkaitan dengan hujan dalam mitologi Jepang.
statement.en: Zennyo Ryūō is a rain-associated dragon deity in Japanese mythology.

claims.quote: According to Japanese Buddhist tradition, the priest Kūkai made Zennyo Ryūō appear in 824 AD during a famous rainmaking contest at the Kyoto Imperial Palace.

statement.id: Menurut tradisi Buddha Jepang, Kūkai memunculkan naga ini pada tahun 824 di Istana Kekaisaran Kyoto dalam lomba doa hujan yang terkenal.
statement.en: According to Japanese Buddhist tradition, Kūkai made the dragon appear in 824 at the Kyoto Imperial Palace in a famous rainmaking contest.

claims.quote: The dragon name Zennyo Ryūō is written in Japanese as 善 zen "good, goodness; virtuous", 女 nyo "woman; female" or 如 nyo "like; as if; be like; thus" (differentiated with the "mouth radical" 口), and 龍王 ryūō or 竜王 "dragon king".

statement.id: Namanya memuat 龍王, ungkapan yang berarti raja naga; 善 berarti baik.
statement.en: The name contains 龍王, meaning dragon king; 善 means good.

claims.quote: Zennyo is a common theme in Japanese art, usually depicted as a small dragon but sometimes as a human, either male or female, with a dragon's tail.

statement.id: Karya seni menggambarkannya sebagai naga kecil atau manusia berekor naga.
statement.en: Art represents the deity as a small dragon or as a human with a dragon’s tail.

claims.quote: The best-known appearance of Zennyo was during an 824 CE Buddhist rainmaking competition at the Shinsen'en or Shinzen'en 神泉苑 "Divine Spring Garden" in Kyoto. The scholar priest Kūkai or Kōbō-Daishi (774–835 CE), founder of Shingon "True Word" Buddhism, and his rival priest Shubin 守敏 held a rain-sutra recitation contest.

statement.id: Kemunculan Zennyo yang paling terkenal terjadi pada lomba doa hujan Buddhis tahun 824 di Shinsen'en (神泉苑, "Taman Mata Air Ilahi") di Kyoto, ketika pendeta Kūkai (Kōbō-Daishi), pendiri Buddhisme Shingon, dan saingannya Shubin (守敏) mengadakan lomba pembacaan sutra hujan.
statement.en: Zennyo's best-known appearance was at the 824 Buddhist rainmaking competition at the Shinsen'en (神泉苑, "Divine Spring Garden") in Kyoto, where the priest Kūkai (Kōbō-Daishi), founder of Shingon Buddhism, and his rival Shubin (守敏) held a rain-sutra recitation contest.

claims.quote: Zennyo is worshipped at the Zennyo Ryūō-sha 善女竜王社 Shinto shrine on an island in the Shinsen'en, reached by crossing the Hōsei-bashi 法成橋 "Dharma Completion Bridge".

statement.id: Zennyo dipuja di kuil Shinto Zennyo Ryūō-sha (善女竜王社) pada sebuah pulau di Shinsen'en, yang dicapai dengan menyeberangi Jembatan Hōsei-bashi (法成橋).
statement.en: Zennyo is worshipped at the Shinto shrine Zennyo Ryūō-sha (善女竜王社) on an island in the Shinsen'en, reached by crossing the Hōsei-bashi (法成橋) bridge.

claims.quote: The 835 CE Goyuigō 御遺告, which records Kūkai's last words, first describes Zennyo (Fowler 1997:154) as, "a golden snake measuring eight sun 寸 (approx. 24 cm) riding on the head of a dragon measuring nine shaku 尺 (approx. 2.7 m).

statement.id: 御遺告 tahun 835, yang mencatat kata-kata terakhir Kūkai, pertama kali menggambarkan Zennyo sebagai ular emas sepanjang delapan sun (sekitar 24 cm) yang menunggangi kepala naga sepanjang sembilan shaku (sekitar 2,7 m).
statement.en: The 835 御遺告 (Goyuigō), which records Kūkai's last words, first describes Zennyo as a golden snake eight sun (about 24 cm) long riding on the head of a dragon nine shaku (about 2.7 m) long.

claims.quote: Some versions of this Kūkai story record Zennyo coming from Mount Murō and others from Lake Anavatapta, which is at the center of the world in Buddhist cosmology.

statement.id: Sebagian versi kisah Kūkai ini menyebut Zennyo datang dari Gunung Murō, sedangkan yang lain dari Danau Anavatapta yang berada di pusat dunia dalam kosmologi Buddhis.
statement.en: Some versions of this Kūkai story have Zennyo coming from Mount Murō and others from Lake Anavatapta, at the center of the world in Buddhist cosmology.

claims.quote: Zennyo or Zentatsu 善達 supposedly lived in the Ryūketsu 龍穴 "Dragon Hole/Cave" on Murōyama 室生山 "Mount Murō" in Nara Prefecture, which was an ancient locale of Japanese dragon worship and rainmaking ceremonies.

statement.id: Zennyo atau Zentatsu (善達) konon tinggal di Ryūketsu (龍穴, "gua naga") di Gunung Murō (室生山) di Prefektur Nara, tempat kuno pemujaan naga dan upacara pemanggil hujan di Jepang.
statement.en: Zennyo or Zentatsu (善達) supposedly lived in the Ryūketsu (龍穴, "dragon cave") on Mount Murō (室生山) in Nara Prefecture, an ancient site of dragon worship and rainmaking ceremonies in Japan.

claims.quote: Kokan Shiren's c. 1322 CE Genkō Shakusho "the Genkō era History of Buddhism" has a story about the priest Keien 慶圓 (1143–1223 CE) encountering a beautiful woman who was actually a shapeshifting Zennyo.

statement.id: Genkō Shakusho karya Kokan Shiren (sekitar 1322) memuat kisah pendeta Keien (慶圓, 1143-1223) yang bertemu seorang perempuan cantik yang sebenarnya Zennyo yang mengubah wujud.
statement.en: Kokan Shiren's Genkō Shakusho (c. 1322) has a story of the priest Keien (慶圓, 1143-1223) meeting a beautiful woman who was in fact a shapeshifting Zennyo.

claims.quote: she answered: "I am the Dragon Zennyo". ... It proved to be a claw, more than ten shaku long, which spread a five-coloured light.

statement.id: Dalam kisah itu perempuan tersebut menjawab "Aku adalah Naga Zennyo", dan jari kelingkingnya yang terulur ternyata sebuah cakar lebih dari sepuluh shaku panjangnya yang memancarkan cahaya lima warna.
statement.en: In that story the woman answers "I am the Dragon Zennyo", and the little finger she stretches out proves to be a claw more than ten shaku long that spreads a five-coloured light.

claims.quote: 善女龍王（ぜんにょりゅうおう）は雨乞いの対象である竜王のうちの一尊。「善如龍王」とも表記される。

statement.id: Zennyo Ryūō (善女龍王) adalah salah satu raja naga yang menjadi sasaran doa meminta hujan, dan juga ditulis 「善如龍王」.
statement.en: Zennyo Ryūō (善女龍王) is one of the dragon kings who are objects of rain-praying, and is also written 「善如龍王」.

claims.quote: 調べると空海の名声を妬む守敏により国中の龍神が瓶に閉じ込められていた。しかしただ1体、善女龍王だけは守敏の手から逃れていたので天竺の無熱池（むねっち）から呼び寄せて国中に大雨を降らせたという。

statement.id: Setelah diselidiki, dewa naga seluruh negeri ternyata dikurung dalam guci oleh 守敏 yang iri pada nama baik 空海; hanya Zennyo Ryūō yang lolos dari tangan 守敏, sehingga ia dipanggil dari kolam 無熱池 di India dan konon menurunkan hujan lebat ke seluruh negeri.
statement.en: On investigation, the dragon gods of the whole land had been shut in a pitcher by 守敏, who envied 空海's fame; only Zennyo Ryūō had escaped 守敏's hand, so he was summoned from the pond 無熱池 in India and is said to have sent heavy rain over the whole country.

claims.quote: この弘法（空海）の雨乞いの際にやってきた善女龍王は、八大竜王のひとり阿那婆達多龍王の一族で、阿耨達池（あのくだっち）より阿那婆達多によって連れてこられたとされる。

statement.id: Zennyo Ryūō yang datang pada doa hujan 弘法 (空海) disebut keluarga 阿那婆達多龍王, salah satu dari Delapan Raja Naga, dan dikatakan dibawa dari kolam 阿耨達池 oleh 阿那婆達多.
statement.en: The Zennyo Ryūō who came at 弘法 (空海)'s rain-praying is said to belong to the family of 阿那婆達多龍王, one of the Eight Dragon Kings, and to have been brought from the pond 阿耨達池 by 阿那婆達多.

claims.quote: 「善女」とあるが、像容は男神像で表現されることもあり女神であるとは限らない。

statement.id: Meski disebut 「善女」, rupanya kadang digambarkan sebagai dewa laki-laki, jadi belum tentu seorang dewi.
statement.en: Although it says 「善女」, its image is sometimes shown as a male deity, so it is not necessarily a goddess.

topic.en: Zennyo's origin in the Kūkai story

summary.id: Sebagian versi: Zennyo datang dari Gunung Murō.
summary.en: Some versions: Zennyo comes from Mount Murō.

summary.id: Versi lain: dari Danau Anavatapta, atau kolam 無熱池 di India.
summary.en: Other versions: from Lake Anavatapta, or the pond 無熱池 in India.

summary.id: Gambar kadang berupa naga kecil atau manusia laki-laki maupun perempuan berekor naga.
summary.en: Art shows a small dragon or a human, male or female, with a dragon's tail.

summary.id: Walau disebut 「善女」, rupanya kadang berupa dewa laki-laki.
summary.en: Although called 「善女」, the image is sometimes a male deity.
